title: Heuristic Funnel Lifecycle — lanelet triggers & experiment seeds
summary: Working notes for defining lifecycle rules that move requests/sessions through fidelity lanes based on runtime signals; includes rough PRD sections, user stories, test matrix, and open questions.
content:
Objective and framing:

This is a rough sketch for a small product/infra feature: a rules-driven heuristic funnel that promotes/demotes requests and sessions across ‘fidelity lanes’ (high, medium, low) at inference time. The funnel should be lightweight (evaluated in edge policy layer or gateway) and able to run experiments and rollouts without changing model code. Goal is to reduce cost tail while preserving perceived quality and to provide a controllable knob for progressive rollout of new models/quant settings.

Why:
- Observed: 15–25% of requests could be served in cheaper lanes (short prompts, trivial completions) with minimal quality regression but we lack a reliable runtime classifier to route them.
- This funnel provides deterministic, debuggable heuristics driven by signals we already have (prompt length, user tier, historical pass rate, recent eval score, latency SLO headroom).
- Enables canary/experiment patterns (e.g., send 10% of a user cohort to medium lane for 30m and measure downstream engagement).

High-level behavior:
- Input signals (per-request and per-session): prompt token count, input type tag, user plan, recent error rate, historical rollback flag, KV cache hit rate, model-variant compatibility map, time-of-day, observed latency headroom.
- Lane definitions: HIGH (full model, highest quality, highest cost), MID (quantized variant, smaller context, aggressive caching), LOW (short-response fast path / heuristic template-responses / cached canned answers).
- Transitions: rules + soft thresholds. Each session/request gets a lane decision and a ‘reassess window’ TTL (e.g., 30s or N messages). Reassessment may promote or demote.
- Safety: allow immediate override via explicit customer pins or safety tags. Always fallback to HIGH on hallucination-detection or safety triggers.

Rough PRD outline (minimal viable set):
- Feature: Runtime Heuristic Funnel v0.1
  - Config: set of per-tenant rules (simple predicates + weight), global default policy, override flags (pinned model/fidelity), traffic-sampling for experiments.
  - API: Console UI toggle + JSON rule editor (basic predicates: token_count < X, user_plan in [free,basic,premium], last_response_quality >= 0.9), and SDK header to tag important requests.
  - Runtime: stateless decision service with Redis-backed ephemeral counters (for short windows) and metrics emitted per-decision.
  - Experimentation: built-in sampling (percent-of-requests) and cohort selectors (by user segment).

User stories (prioritized):
- As an ML engineer, I want to define a temporary rule that sends 5% of queries under 30 tokens to MID lane, so I can evaluate latency and quality trade-offs for quantized models.
- As a product manager, I want an easy rollback switch to force all traffic to HIGH lane for a tenant if regressions are detected.
- As an SRE, I want per-lane metrics (requests, avg latency, 95p latency, error rate, quality delta) in the Console so I can enforce SLOs and alarms.
- As a platform engineer, I want the decision logic to be fast (<1ms) and idempotent so it can live as an Envoy/gateway filter for hosted traffic.

Acceptance criteria (v0.1):
- Decision latency median < 1ms; p95 < 3ms under 1k rps baseline.
- Console allows creating/activating a rule and sampling a cohort; rule activation emits a tagged metric.
- Canary running: ability to route 1–10% of matched requests to MID/LOW and observe quality delta in evaluation events in 1 hour.
- Safety override: single-button rollback per-tenant that returns traffic to HIGH and pauses experiments.

Signals and metrics to capture:
- Per-decision: lane_assigned, rule_id (or default), reason_tags (e.g., token_count, cached_answer), decision_latency_ms.
- Per-lane: qps, avg_token_cost, avg_latency_ms, error_rate, semantic_quality_score (from micro-evals), user-engagement delta (if available).
- Experiment targets: compare matched vs. control via uplift metrics (completion length, user follow-up rate, downstream conversions).

Implementation notes and tech constraints: 
- Keep the decision service tiny and deterministic. Prefer a lua/wasm filter in the proxy that evaluates simple rules and emits counters. If a rule requires state (sample windows), consult a small cache (redis or in-proxy counters).
- Avoid heavy ML at v0 — start with heuristics and deterministic signals. Later add a lightweight classifier as an opt-in hybrid.
- On private deployments, rules should be editable via config files or a private console sync; avoid telemetry leakage.

Experiment matrix (seed ideas):
- Short-prompt sample: token_count < 24 => sample to MID at 1%, 5%, 10% bands for 48h. Measure quality delta and error rates.
- Cold-user band: users with < 3 requests in last 7d => route to MID low-sample to test cold behavior.
- Cost-savings band: send cached question patterns to LOW lane and measure percent served entirely from cache + user satisfaction.

UX/Console sketches (notes to self):
- Rule list: name, predicate preview, sample percent, active toggle, last_changed, matched-rps preview.
- Quick rollback: per-tenant pill on top of funnel page that forces HIGH lane.
- Visual experiment overlay: timeline of sample activation and parallel metrics of matched vs control.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Quality regressions not immediately visible -> mitigation: short sampling windows + conservative sample rates + automatic rollback triggers (semantic quality delta > threshold).
- Risk: Decision service becomes a latency hotspot -> mitigation: wasm/lua filter + local counters, fallback decisions if dependency unavailable.
- Risk: Too many rules complexity -> mitigation: surface rule conflicts and priority order; provide simple mode (tiered defaults) and advanced mode.

Open questions / TODOs: 
- Which semantic-quality signal is cheap enough to use in runtime experiment monitoring? (micro-evals vs. user telemetry).
- How to represent composite predicates in Console without scaring non-engineers? Suggest pattern library (token_count, user_plan, cached_hit, kv_cache_age, last_quality).
- How to model per-tenant quotas and cost accounting when lane changes alter billing? Need finance input on attribution.
- Should lane transitions be sticky at session-level or per-request? Default: sticky per session for N messages with periodic reassess.
- Privacy: ensure that any telemetry used respects tenant data boundaries and PII rules.

Next steps (short):
1) Quick tech spike: implement a proto lua filter that reads token_count and returns lane header (one engineer, 2 days).
2) Wire simple metrics pipeline for decision tags (1 engineer, 3 days).
3) Design Console wireframe for creating a single rule (PM + designer, 3–4 days).
4) Run two 48h samples (short-prompt, cached patterns) and collect quality deltas.

Notes to self (brain dump):
- Keep the API for rules versioned and human-friendly (JSON-ish DSL with limited operators).
- Document safe defaults for new tenants (no sampling on high-sensitivity customers).
- Consider a ‘fidelity debug’ header that forces a lane and prints decision_reason in logs for field debugging.

Scratch examples (rule DSL idea):
- { "id": "short-prompt-mid-1", "predicate": "token_count < 24", "sample_pct": 0.05, "target_lane": "MID", "sticky_ttl": 180 }
- { "id": "cache-first-low", "predicate": "cached_answer == true && user_plan != 'enterprise'", "sample_pct": 1.0, "target_lane": "LOW", "sticky_ttl": 60 }

Final-ish thought: v0 should be humble — prove the operational model with tiny, conservative experiments and real metrics. If we can reliably show 10–15% unit-cost saving on a few tenants with imperceptible quality impact, this becomes an easy productized knob for customers and for internal cost ops.

-- ish
